figmaExecutionNotes: Keep section padding compact and consistent to prevent unnecessary whitespace.
Use the provided copy verbatim; do not rewrite hero, trust, or feature text.
Prioritize trust bar visibility immediately after hero.
Use one design system for all feature sections to maintain consistency and speed of Figma assembly.
Do not fabricate testimonials, news, forms, or pricing numbers because they are not supported by the input.
Ensure mobile stacks hero content vertically, trust remains compact, and feature grids collapse to single-column cards.
Maintain brand fit with Zoho Workplace by using a warm collaboration palette rather than a generic corporate blue theme.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed white-to-soft-grey mesh gradient hero with subtle grid lines and orange glow accents. Place a tilted enterprise workspace dashboard cluster as layered floating cards instead of a standard side image, so the composition feels operational and premium. Keep the hero highly structured: bold 64px H1, compact subheadline, and a trust strip below the CTAs. Make the next section dark with light text for contrast, then alternate feature sections between light and dark treatments. Add decorative orbs in the hero and faint circuit/grid motifs in at least two sections. CTA buttons must be solid Techjockey orange with rounded geometry and strong hover contrast.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a content-first split hero, then shift immediately into a logo trust band to keep warm traffic continuity without visual fatigue.
Use a 3-step process section after the hero instead of a generic features block to satisfy the warm-traffic sequence and create momentum.
Alternate product sections between spotlight-plus-grid, split-panel-list, and a compact marquee-style integration strip so no two adjacent blocks feel visually identical.
Place the testimonial section as a carousel because there are 4+ testimonials, creating motion before the final CTA.
Keep the final pricing/CTA area highly focused and card-centered to close with a clear conversion moment rather than another information-heavy block.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprise Teams | Unified Email & Collaboration Suite
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Workplace for enterprises: a unified email, chat, docs, meetings, and file-sharing suite with strong security, seamless collaboration, and easy onboarding.

sections.backgroundTreatment: clean white canvas with subtle workspace-panel accents and a compact benefit row under the CTA
sections.designNote: Make the hero content-first to match the ad message and answer all three hero questions immediately: what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the right side as a polished enterprise workspace mockup with email, chat, docs, meetings, and storage tiles. Use the supplied headline and subheadline, but tighten the visual hierarchy so the CTA 'Get started' is unmistakable and the supporting line feels like credibility chips rather than body copy.

Use an early logo-first trust band with 3-6 recognizable enterprise logos if available; if not, fall back to the provided metric strip. Since only one proof cue is explicitly available, present the social proof as a compact static band with a strong label and a single highlighted business-count metric. Keep this section visually denser and more compressed than the hero to build confidence without slowing the scroll.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: Get up and running in under 60 seconds

sections.designNote: Insert a dedicated 3-step how-it-works section because the traffic is warm and expects quick clarity. Keep it under 60 seconds, visually simple, and operational: 1) choose a plan, 2) set up email and users, 3) start collaborating. Use a split-panel rhythm with one strong visual panel and a concise numbered list so the section feels action-oriented, not explanatory.

Treat the first product block as the main feature spotlight and keep the rest of the product sections as alternating supporting panels. Because there are multiple product sections and some include 4+ features, avoid a flat grid; instead use spotlight-plus-grid for the first block, split-panel-list for the integration block, and a compact accordion-with-visual treatment for the enterprise/security insight block if it needs depth. Emphasize the click-driving features first: unified workspace, real-time collaboration, anywhere access, and AI productivity. Maintain strong visual contrast between adjacent blocks by alternating white and light-grey backgrounds and flipping media alignment.

Use a centered highlighted pricing card to keep the conversion moment direct and enterprise-appropriate. Present the included enterprise-grade package details as a clean checklist with the Get started CTA in solid accent orange at full opacity. Keep the card compact and decisive rather than comparison-heavy, since the page is already long-form and the pricing content reads like a bundled value summary.

Render testimonials as a carousel because there are 4+ quotes. Keep the cards generous but not oversized, and rotate between IT, operations, and systems perspectives to reinforce enterprise relevance. This section should feel credibility-led rather than promotional, with subtle motion and minimal CTA pressure.

Use the form as the final conversion anchor, framed as a secure digital workspace action area. Keep it centered and floating for emphasis, with only the essential fields and a single primary CTA labeled Get started. Mobile CTA must be full-width and solid accent orange. This should feel like the strongest conversion surface on the page.

If additional media or partner marks exist, show them as a compact horizontal logo strip; otherwise omit this as a separate visual block and merge its function into the trust section. If retained, keep it thin and non-intrusive so it does not compete with the final CTA.

blueprint.designPersonality: A clean, operations-led enterprise landing page with strong logo credibility, compact content blocks, and an efficient workspace feel. The page should feel organized, trustworthy, and implementation-ready, with the orange brand accent used sparingly but decisively for CTAs, highlights, and confidence cues.

Learn from the brrand

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and enterprise-oriented, so 48px keeps it strong without wrapping too aggressively on desktop.

colours.colourReason: The palette is derived strictly from Techjockey brand colors: orange as the primary CTA and identity color, white as the main canvas, near-black for text, and soft grey for section separation. This keeps the page aligned with the brand reference and avoids introducing unrelated hues.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column hero with logo lockup above a centered headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefit list using tick icons; strong top-of-page emphasis with no visible media split in the main hero.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Long-form landing page built as stacked content blocks separated by clear vertical spacing; hero first, then lead capture form, then feature-led informational sections; minimal horizontal complexity and no apparent tabbed navigation.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-first content cards with simple rectangular containers, light borders or subtle elevation, and text-first hierarchy; cards are likely used for form and feature grouping rather than decorative showcase panels.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion is concentrated in a lead form rather than multiple high-friction buttons; CTA strategy favors one dominant action near the top with supporting microcopy and repeated form submission intent lower in the page.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module visible in the reference structure; pricing is likely deferred or omitted in favor of consultation/lead capture.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in provided reference, but likely a standard informational footer with corporate links and support details rather than a conversion-heavy footer.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible hero; emphasis is on text and icon bullets. Any media would be secondary, likely used as supporting imagery or product context rather than immersive video or gallery.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature sections use headline-plus-description intros followed by multi-item lists of benefits; structure supports progressive disclosure through stacked sections with repeated thematic grouping (core features, business value, integrations).
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead generation form placed directly after the hero in a prominent card. The form appears dense but modular, with hidden metadata fields and a primary user input area designed for qualification and routing.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static informational layout with no evident motion system in the visible structure; if motion exists, it is limited to standard form or slider behavior not exposed in the snippet.
designNotes: Optimize for enterprise lead generation with high trust and low friction.
Keep copy blocks short and scannable with benefit-led bullets.
Use strong section separation and generous whitespace to support long-form reading.
Prioritize form visibility early in the page over extended storytelling.
Avoid reliance on complex navigation patterns; use linear scroll progression instead.

HARD BRAND DESIGN RULES:
- Use brand URL section patterns for layout inspiration.
- Match brand-like spacing rhythm, CTA shape, card style, and section composition.
- If user requested light theme, prefer brand page light surfaces and avoid forced dark/orange theme.
- Do not use unrelated category default colors if brand reference shows a clear visual style.
- Do not use irrelevant scraped media just because it is available.

mustHaveMoments: Logo lockup and trust badge above the fold
Centered hero with concise value proposition and dual CTA
Immediate proof strip highlighting 100,000+ businesses globally
Feature blocks focused on enterprise productivity, security, and collaboration
Pricing/inclusion card with clear enterprise deliverables and migration assistance
Testimonial carousel or stacked quotes to reinforce adoption confidence
Security-focused final CTA block emphasizing privacy-first, SSO, MFA, and spam protection
avoidPatterns: Split hero with unnecessary media gap
Excess whitespace between sections or inside feature cards
Tab-heavy or carousel-heavy layouts that hide content
Generic stock imagery if it weakens trust or adds visual clutter
Mismatched copy or paraphrased content that diverges from the supplied inputs
designStrategy.reasoning: This is a single-product enterprise lead-gen page for a well-known collaboration suite, so the page should push fast trust, clear value, and immediate conversion. Since visitors trust logos most, the dominant trust signal should be a logos-first proof treatment near the hero, followed by compact social proof and testimonials. The content is long and feature-rich, so a dense stacked narrative is better than airy or editorial spacing; it keeps the user moving without dead zones. The hero should be centered and message-led with a strong headline, short support copy, and two CTAs to accommodate both direct action and trial intent. The page should feel safe and enterprise-ready rather than flashy, with security and reliability emphasized in the final CTA block. A proof-led structure best fits the mix of stats, testimonials, and enterprise utility, while avoiding the empty-space and content-mismatch issues noted in prior feedback.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers

Desktop.notes: Use the exact hero content from contentMap. Left text stack: headline, subheadline, supportingLine, primary CTA, secondary CTA. Right side should be a clean product-relevant visual treatment only if available from assets; otherwise keep a strong centered visual block or abstract brand panel, but do not introduce unsupported UI claims. CTA styling: primary solid accent, secondary outline/ghost. Maintain tight spacing to avoid empty whitespace. Hero background should follow warmth-people primary color with light text.

This is the dominant trust signal. Use the trust badge line 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally' as the primary element. Build as a horizontal logo/trust row with badge styling, customer count stat, and divider-separated items. Keep compact and prominent directly below hero. If no customer logos are provided, use the trust badge and count stat only; do not fabricate logos.

Render the four features exactly as provided under 'Why Choose Zoho Workplace?'. Use 2x2 on desktop or a 4-card grid optimized for compactness. Each card should use the standard feature card pattern with title and description. No placeholder icons; if no icons are available, use text-first cards with a consistent top spacing and minimal whitespace.

Render the four features exactly as provided under 'Unlock Your Business Growth with Zoho Workplace'. Keep the same card system for consistency, but vary the section header and subtle background separation if needed. Do not add extra bullets or claims beyond the supplied copy.

Render the integration categories exactly as provided: Zoho Apps, Analytics, Accounting & Finance, Automation. Use compact cards because several feature descriptions are short. Keep the section dense and avoid excessive vertical padding. Do not invent logos or app badges unless sourced assets exist.

Only include a cart/pricing card because design memory explicitly flags it as a missing recurring requirement. Since no pricing data is provided in contentMap, create a safe conversion card structure without pricing numerals: headline, brief value statement, checklist of included enterprise benefits inferred only from provided content, primary CTA 'Get Started', secondary CTA 'Get Your Free Trial', and trust line. Keep it clearly labeled as an inquiry/trial action card, not a fabricated price panel.
